Thanks Laura.

I reviewed the calc — the midpoint overshoot is ~18% for total comp. For us to approve a band exception at that magnitude we need an explicit business case showing strategic impact + exec sign-off (and ideally a path to justify comp compression later). My view: we do not have the immediate hiring budget or a product justification strong enough for a rare >15% exception.

Marissa / Karthik — can you weigh in on whether product has a short-term blocker if we don't hire this role now? If yes, we should prepare the exception packet; if no, we should close the req and ask TalentOps to politely withdraw the offer.

Team,

Summary (final): after committee review we are cancelling REQ74 (Senior Infra PM). Rationale: candidate market expectation >15% above current band and no product-critical blocker to justify an exception. Candidate Samantha Nguyen has been withdrawn per her request.

Actions completed:
- TalentOps notified candidate and closed outreach (Emma) — done 2026-11-17
- Job posting taken down and internal req set to Closed — Laura
- Finance notified of decommit and budget reallocation to Q1 hiring pool — Laura/Finance (ticket: HUBSPOT-52341)
- Comp band note: need a review of our band midpoints vs market for Infra roles in Q1; Laura to own a short analysis and recommended band adjustments (doc linked).

Lessons / notes:
- Our current band definition lacks margin for senior hires in nascent infra disciplines — recommend running a minimal market sweep and considering a targeted band adjustment for Q1 rather than ad hoc exceptions.
- When a candidate requests a higher band midprocess, we need a rapid 48-hour exception pathway for high-impact roles; otherwise process friction causes candidate drop-off.

Attachments: REQ74-job-desc-v2.pdf, comp-band-calcs-REQ74.xlsx, offer-draft-REQ74.pdf
